/-!
# Erdős Problem 53

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/53](https://www.erdosproblems.com/53)
- [Er77c] Erdős, Paul, *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III*. Number theory
  day (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ., New York, 1976) (1977), 43-72.
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [ErSz83] Erdős, P. and Szemerédi, E., *On sums and products of integers*. Studies in pure
  mathematics (1983), 213-218.
- [Er91] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number
  theory*. Graph theory, combinatorics, and applications, Vol. 1 (Kalamazoo, MI, 1988) (1991),
  397-406.
- [Er97] Erdős, Paul, *Problems in number theory*. New Zealand J. Math. (1997), 155-160.
- [Er97e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. Math. Japon. (1997), 527-537.
- [Ch03] Chang, M.-C., *The Erdős-Szemerédi problem on sum set and product set*. Annals of Math.
  (2003), 939-957.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos53

/-- The integers which are either the sum or the product of (one or more) distinct elements of
`A`. -/
def sumsAndProducts (A : Finset ℤ) : Finset ℤ :=
  (A.powerset.erase ∅).image (fun B => ∑ b ∈ B, b) ∪
    (A.powerset.erase ∅).image (fun B => ∏ b ∈ B, b)

/--
Let $A$ be a finite set of integers. Is it true that, for every $k$, if $\lvert A\rvert$ is
sufficiently large depending on $k$, then there are least $\lvert A\rvert^k$ many integers which
are either the sum or product of distinct elements of $A$?

Asked by Erdős and Szemerédi [ErSz83]. Solved in this form by Chang [Ch03].

Erdős and Szemerédi proved that there exist arbitrarily large sets $A$ such that the number of
integers which are the sum or product of distinct elements of $A$ is at most
$$\exp\left(c (\log \lvert A\rvert)^2\log\log\lvert A\rvert\right)$$
for some constant $c>0$.

See also [52](https://www.erdosproblems.com/52).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos53.lean#L3084"]
theorem erdos_53 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ k : ℕ, ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ A : Finset ℤ, N ≤ A.card →
    A.card ^ k ≤ (sumsAndProducts A).card := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős and Szemerédi [ErSz83] proved that there exist arbitrarily large sets $A$ such that the
number of integers which are the sum or product of distinct elements of $A$ is at most
$$\exp\left(c (\log \lvert A\rvert)^2\log\log\lvert A\rvert\right)$$
for some constant $c>0$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_53.variants.upper : ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ A : Finset ℤ, N ≤ A.card ∧
    ((sumsAndProducts A).card : ℝ) ≤
      Real.exp (c * Real.log A.card ^ 2 * Real.log (Real.log A.card)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos53

findings.description:
The variant bounds the count by `Real.exp (c * Real.log A.card ^ 2 * Real.log (Real.log A.card))`, i.e. exp(c (log|A|)^2 · log log|A|). The docstring says this is what Erdős and Szemerédi [ErSz83] proved. Their Theorem 2 actually divides by log log: g(n) < exp(c₃ log²n / log log n). So the Lean states a strictly weaker claim than the cited result. The two exponents differ by a factor of (log log|A|)^2, which tends to infinity.

Lean checks (in /workspace/review/scratch2.lean, no sorry):
- The E–S form, with `/ Real.log (Real.log A.card)`, implies the file's statement (`ESdiv_imp_fileVariant`).
- For every C and every c > 0, eventually C·log²x/log log x ≤ c·log²x·log log x.

The converse fails in content. The file's bound is already met by the elementary family A = {∏_{i∈S} p_i : S ⊆ [J]}: here |A| = 2^J, the subset sums are exp(O(J log J)), and the subset products number at most (2^{J-1}+1)^J = exp(O(log²|A|)). So the Lean statement would still hold if the true order were exp(Θ(log²|A|)). The E–S bound is sharp: Chang's Theorem 2 gives ln g(k) ≍ (ln k)²/ln ln k. As written, the variant misstates both the E–S result and the known order of magnitude.

The slip is copied verbatim from the erdosproblems.com remark. The same wrong formula appears in the prose of the `erdos_53` docstring and of this variant's docstring.
findings.source_evidence: [ErSz83], p. 213–214 (https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1983-18.pdf, scanned; I OCR'd it and re-read the line at 4× upscaling): "Denote now by g(n) the largest integer so that for every (a_1,…,a_n) there are at least g(n) distinct integers of the form (3) Σ ε_i a_i, Π a_i^{ε_i} (ε_i = 0 or 1) … We prove Theorem 2. g(n) < exp(c_3 log²n / log log n)." Chang, Annals 157 (2003), p. 941, eq. (0.15) (https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v157-n3-p07.pdf): "Theorem (Erdős–Szemerédi). Let g(k) ≡ min_{|A|=k}{|A[1]|+|A{1}|}. There is a constant c such that g(k) < e^{c (ln k)²/ln ln k}." Chang's Theorem 2 (0.21): k^{(1+ε) ln k/ln ln k} > g(k) > k^{(1/8−ε) ln k/ln ln k}. Her abstract: "ln g(k) ∼ (ln k)²/ln ln k". Section 3 of Chang's paper repeats the E–S construction with the same bound. By contrast, erdosproblems.com/latex/53 reads "…is at most \[\exp\left(c (\log \lvert A\rvert)^2\log\log\lvert A\rvert\right)\] for some constant $c>0$"; the file copies this slip.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the bound to `Real.exp (c * Real.log A.card ^ 2 / Real.log (Real.log A.card))`. In the docstrings of both `erdos_53` and `erdos_53.variants.upper`, change the displayed formula to $\exp\left(c\,\frac{(\log\lvert A\rvert)^2}{\log\log\lvert A\rvert}\right)$. There is no junk-value problem: log log|A| > 0 for |A| ≥ 3, and the `∀ N, ∃ A, N ≤ A.card` form lets the witness be taken large. Optionally add Chang's matching lower bound, exp(c' log²|A| / log log|A|) ≤ count for all large A, as a further solved variant.

reformulations.difference: `sumsAndProducts` ranges only over nonempty subsets, so the empty sum 0 and empty product 1 are not counted, and the Lean asks for `A.card ^ k ≤ card`. [ErSz83] (3) and Chang (0.6)–(0.7) use ε_i ∈ {0,1}, so the empty subset is included, and ask for g(n) > n^k. The linked formal proof (plby, L3084) also uses subsets including ∅: Mathlib `Finset.subsetSum` ∪ subset products.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The all-subsets value set contains `sumsAndProducts A` and is contained in insert 0 (insert 1 (sumsAndProducts A)), so the two cardinalities differ by at most 2. One direction is monotonicity. For the other, apply the all-subsets statement with exponent k+1 and threshold max N 3: then |A|^k + 2 ≤ 3|A|^k ≤ |A|^{k+1} ≤ |sumsAndProducts A| + 2. Strict versus non-strict inequality is absorbed the same way, using exponent k+1. So the linked formal proof establishes an equivalent statement.

reformulations.difference: A ranges over all finite sets of integers (`Finset ℤ`), as on erdosproblems.com and in Chang's abstract ("over all sets A ⊂ Z"). [ErSz83] instead takes 1 ≤ a_1 < … < a_n, and Chang's Conjecture 2 and her proofs are stated for A ⊂ ℕ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The ℤ version implies the positive-integer version trivially. Conversely, for A ⊂ ℤ with |A| = n, either P = A ∩ ℤ_{>0} or Q = A ∩ ℤ_{<0} has at least (n−1)/2 elements. Subset sums and products of P (or Q) are subset sums and products of A. The subset sums of Q are the negatives of those of −Q, and the subset products of Q equal those of −Q up to sign, so |S(Q)| ≥ |S(−Q)|/2. Applying the positive version with a larger exponent (k+1 or 2k) absorbs these constant factors for large n. This is exactly `integer_resolution_of_positive_naturals` in the linked plby Lean proof.

review.notes:
`erdos_53` (answer(True), research solved, formal_proof) is faithful. The quantifier order (∀ k ∃ N ∀ A) is right, the domain `Finset ℤ` is right, and the definition behaves as expected on small cases (`#eval`: sumsAndProducts {1,2,3} = {1,…,6}; ∅ ↦ ∅). The status agrees with the site ('PROVED (LEAN) … solved in the affirmative') and with the teorth database ('proved (Lean)'). The formal_proof link points at plby's `erdos_53`, which counts all subsets including the empty one. I proved in Lean that this is equivalent to the file's statement (`main_equiv`, /workspace/review/scratch3.lean).

The one defect is the log log slip in the variant. It is inherited verbatim from erdosproblems.com, so the website remark likely needs the same correction. The primary paper ([ErSz83], Theorem 2) and the solution paper (Chang, eq. (0.15), Theorem 2 and Section 3) both have division by log log n.

How I read the sources: erdosproblems.com is behind a Cloudflare challenge, so I read it through the r.jina.ai reader, including the /latex/53 source view. The E–S paper is image-only; I installed tesseract/poppler system-wide to OCR it. Nothing under /opt/formal-conjectures was modified. The pre-existing lakefile.toml/run changes predate this session.

Not consulted: the other Erdős sources in the module docstring ([Er77c], [ErGr80], [Er91], [Er97], [Er97e]). The Rényi archive link for [Er77c] leads to a different paper, and the 1990s papers are not in the archive. They were not needed to settle either declaration."

demonstrated.claim: Taking as hypothesis the Erdős–Szemerédi Theorem 2 bound as the source states it (exponent c·log²|A| / log log|A|), the declaration as the file states it (via `type_of%`) follows in about 10 lines; the file's exponent is the source's exponent times (log log|A|)², which tends to infinity, so the declaration claims a weaker bound than the result it attributes to [ErSz83].

submission.summary: trivial_proof.lean takes the variant's type exactly as the file states it (`type_of% @Erdos53.erdos_53.variants.upper`) and proves it in about 10 lines. The hypothesis is the bound Erdős and Szemerédi actually prove in [ErSz83], Theorem 2, which Chang (0.15) quotes the same way: exponent c·log²|A| divided by log log|A|. So the file claims only a weaker bound. Two short facts then show the gap is not a constant factor: the file's exponent equals the source's exponent times (log log|A|)², and log log x → ∞. This is an 'other' demonstration, not a proof or disproof. The declaration is true, so it cannot be refuted, and proving it outright would need a real construction. The file compiles cleanly, and `#print axioms` on a named copy shows only the standard axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound).

trivial_proof.lean:
import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«53»

/-!
Erdős–Szemerédi [ErSz83, Theorem 2] prove `g(n) < exp(c₃ log² n / log log n)`: the exponent is
DIVIDED by `log log n`. Chang (Annals 157 (2003), eq. (0.15)) quotes it the same way, and her
Theorem 2 shows this order is sharp. `Erdos53.erdos_53.variants.upper` MULTIPLIES by
`log log |A|` instead.
-/

open Real

-- Erdos53.erdos_53.variants.upper: the bound the source actually proves (with `/ log log |A|`)
-- implies the file's statement in a few lines, so the file only claims a weaker bound.
example (hES : ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ A : Finset ℤ, N ≤ A.card ∧
      ((Erdos53.sumsAndProducts A).card : ℝ) ≤ exp (c * log A.card ^ 2 / log (log A.card))) :
    type_of% @Erdos53.erdos_53.variants.upper := by
  obtain ⟨c, hc, h⟩ := hES
  refine ⟨c, hc, fun N => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨A, hA, hle⟩ := h (max N ⌈exp (exp 1)⌉₊)
  have hA' : exp (exp 1) ≤ (A.card : ℝ) := Nat.ceil_le.mp ((le_max_right _ _).trans hA)
  have h1 : exp 1 ≤ log A.card := (le_log_iff_exp_le ((exp_pos _).trans_le hA')).2 hA'
  have hM : 1 ≤ log (log A.card) := (le_log_iff_exp_le ((exp_pos _).trans_le h1)).2 h1
  have hX : 0 ≤ c * log A.card ^ 2 := by positivity
  refine ⟨A, (le_max_left _ _).trans hA, hle.trans (exp_le_exp.2 ?_)⟩
  exact (div_le_self hX hM).trans (le_mul_of_one_le_right hX hM)

-- Erdos53.erdos_53.variants.upper: the gap is not a constant factor. The file's exponent is the
-- source's exponent times `(log log |A|)²`, and `log log x → ∞`.
example (c L M : ℝ) (hM : M ≠ 0) : c * L ^ 2 * M = c * L ^ 2 / M * M ^ 2 := by
  field_simp

example : Filter.Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => log (log x)) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop :=
  tendsto_log_atTop.comp tendsto_log_atTop

submission.summary:
In `erdos_53.variants.upper` I changed the bound from `Real.exp (c * Real.log A.card ^ 2 * Real.log (Real.log A.card))` to `Real.exp (c * Real.log A.card ^ 2 / Real.log (Real.log A.card))`. This now matches the result the docstring cites, [ErSz83, Theorem 2]: g(n) < exp(c₃ log²n / log log n), which Chang (0.15) quotes the same way. I fixed the displayed formula in that docstring to match. I also added one sentence citing [ErSz83, Theorem 2] and [Ch03, (0.15)] and noting that erdosproblems.com multiplies by log log |A| instead of dividing; this follows the repo's precedent for noting source typos and should stop a later sync with the website from undoing the fix.

For consistency, I corrected the same formula in the prose of the `erdos_53` docstring. The statement of `erdos_53`, the definition, and all attributes are unchanged.

Checks on a scratch copy of the edited file:
- The new type is definitionally the E–S shape (`rfl`).
- log log n ≠ 0 for n ≥ 2 and log log n > 0 for n ≥ 3, so no division-by-zero junk value can make the `∀ N, ∃ A, N ≤ A.card` statement trivial.
- The corrected claim follows from E–S's construction, which uses positive integers and counts a superset that includes 0 and 1. It is still a real, non-trivial statement.

`lake env lean --json` on the edited file reports only the two `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings. Outside this repository, the erdosproblems.com remark for problem 53 has the same slip and should be corrected upstream.
